title: Finite coefficient triple in Epp elimination
statement: Let $p$ be prime. Let $U\to V\to W$ be injective local maps of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction fields $F\subseteq G\subseteq J$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Assume $U$ and $V$ are complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], the residue field $k=U/\mathfrak m_U$ is algebraically closed (every nonconstant polynomial has a root) of characteristic $p$, $\mathfrak m_U V=\mathfrak m_V$, $J/G$ is finite-dimensional, and, inside $V/\mathfrak m_V$, $k=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\{x^{p^n}:x\in V/\mathfrak m_V\}$. For any injective local map $U\to V$ of discrete valuation rings, with fraction fields $F\subseteq G$, call a finite field extension $H/F$ a weak solution if, writing $U_H$ for the integral closure of $U$ in $H$ and $V_H$ for that of $V$ in $(G\otimes_F H)_{\mathrm{red}}$, every maximal ideal $q$ of $V_H$ has maximal contraction $n=q\cap U_H$, both $(U_H)_n$ and $(V_H)_q$ are discrete valuation rings, and $n(V_H)_q=q(V_H)_q$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Here reduction means quotient by all nilpotents, finite means finite-dimensional over the base field, and local means pulling back the maximal ideal to the maximal ideal. There is a finite weak solution $H/F$ for $U\to W$. If $F$ has characteristic $p$, then for any specified uniformizer $t$ of $U$ the solution can be chosen as the compositum of a finite separable extension of $F$ and $F[t^{1/p^r}]$ for some $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; compositum means the subfield generated by the two embedded fields in a common field. There is no assertion of stability under an arbitrary further extension.

source.place: Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, including its proof by finite normal extension filtrations, the degree-p cases and decreasing ramification level. Prescribed purely inseparable uniformizer roots: last paragraph of that proof and Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, paragraph noting the compositum form over k((t)).

proof.text: First normalize: the given $W$ is the integral closure of $V$ in $J$ and is complete, by finite normalization over the complete DVR $V$. The filtration lemma embeds $J$ in a finite normal $N/G$ and provides a tower with the four indicated types. Any solution for the upper normalization in $N$ descends to $W$ by weak-solution descent. It therefore suffices to treat an arbitrary tower of these types, allowing identity steps and allowing the cyclic prime-to-$p$ case to have a separable residue extension. This slight enlargement is what makes the induction stable under normalized base change.

source.place: Tag 09F8, first three paragraphs of proof.

proof.text: We prove by induction on the length of such a tower that there is a weak solution, for any complete weakly unramified bottom pair with algebraically closed lower residue equal to the upper perfect core. Length zero is solved by $H=F$: the reduction and normalization then return the original DVRs. In each of the four one-step cases we now construct a finite coefficient solution. The constructions below apply to the original bottom pair and to every pair occurring later in the induction.

We will use the following elementary consequence of the existing root-algebra statement. For a DVR $R$ and uniformizer $t$, $R[u]=R[X]/(X^n-t)$ is a DVR with maximal ideal $(u)$ for every $n\geq1$. The monic quotient basis $1,u,\ldots,u^{n-1}$ remains a basis after inverting $t$, so its fraction field is $\operatorname{Frac}(R)[u]$ of degree $n$. A DVR is a PID and hence integrally closed. Since $R[u]$ is integral over $R$, any element of its fraction field integral over $R$ is integral over $R[u]$ and therefore lies in $R[u]$: this is the whole integral closure. Its residue field is $R/(t)$ and $(t)=(u^n)$. If $p\nmid n$, the derivative $nX^{n-1}$ has no common root with $X^n-t$, so this field extension is separable. For $n=1$ these assertions reduce to the identity map.

source.place: Tag 09EV, lemma-pull-root-uniformizer, elementary quotient calculation using existing root-algebra node.

proof.text: For an unramified step the filtration lemma gives equality of the extended maximal ideals. Its composition with $U\to V$ has index one, so take $H=F$. For a cyclic step of degree prime to $p$, write $e$ for its ramification index. The filtration gives $p\nmid e$ and separability of the upper residue over that of $V$. Put $H=F[t^{1/e}]$ for a uniformizer $t$ of $U$. The preceding root calculation gives lower index $e$, degree $e$, and separability. The totally ramified base-change lemma on $U\to V$ gives $V_H=V[t^{1/e}]$ and $U_H\to V_H$ of index one. Apply tame cancellation to $V\to W$ and the finite extension $G[t^{1/e}]/G$: its lower index is $e$ by that same root calculation on $V$, so every upper normalized branch has index one over $V_H$ and thus over $U_H$. For $e=1$ take $H=F$.

source.place: Tag 09F8, cases (d) and (c), using the existing arbitrary-DVR form of Abhyankar.

proof.text: For a purely inseparable step of degree $p$, apply its three-way lemma. Alternative (i) is solved by $F$; alternative (iii) supplies the required separable coefficient solution. In alternative (ii) one has $W=V[t^{1/p}]$. Choose $H=F[t^{1/p}]$. Its lower integral closure is $U[t^{1/p}]$ with uniformizer $t^{1/p}$ by the root calculation of step 3. The reduced tensor $J\otimes_FH$ is $J$ since $t^{1/p}\in J$ and the polynomial $X^p-t$ has just that root in characteristic $p$. The upper normalization is $W$, whose maximal ideal is $(t^{1/p})$ by the same root calculation applied to $V$. Thus the required ideal equality holds.

source.place: Tag 09F8, case (a), and Tag 09EY, three alternatives.

proof.text: For a degree-$p$ Galois step in equal characteristic $p$, the Artin-Schreier coefficient lemma gives a finite separable totally ramified coefficient weak solution. Its hypotheses are exactly the common weak index-one bottom pair and the perfect-core equality in the inductive assertion. There is no assumption of perfection of the upper residue field.

For a degree-$p$ Galois step in mixed characteristic, finite-level preparation first either solves it or produces a degree-$p$ field extension with level $0\leq l<p$. At every subsequent level-lowering base change the bottom pair stays weakly unramified and its upper residue stays unchanged by totally ramified base change; completeness and the algebraically closed lower residue persist by finite normalization and coefficient-field arithmetic. Thus the level-lowering lemma can be reapplied. Level zero gives index one. If $l>p-1$, put $\epsilon=p-l\in(0,1)$; the new level is at most $p-2\epsilon$ unless already solved. While in this interval the positive distance to $p$ therefore at least doubles. Choose an integer $a$ with $2^a\epsilon\geq1$, so after at most $a$ operations the level is at most $p-1$. Thereafter $\max(0,l-1,2l-p)\leq\max(0,l-1)$, and at most $p-1$ more operations reach zero. Compose the finitely many coefficient extensions. Weak-solution descent assembles the successive normalized base changes, so the composite is a finite weak solution.

source.place: Tag 09F8, case (b), mixed characteristic level argument; Tags 09F4 and 09F5.

proof.text: For the induction step, solve the first extension by steps 4-7, obtaining $H_1/F$. Enlarge $H_1$ to a finite normal $N_1/F$ separable over $H_1$ by coefficient-field arithmetic. Its integral closure has residue $k$, so $N_1/H_1$ is totally ramified. Totally ramified base change on each already solved branch preserves index one; by the branchwise normalization clause of weak-solution descent these base-changed rings are exactly the branches over $N_1$, hence $N_1$ still solves the first extension. Choose a branch of the normalized top over $N_1$. Its intermediate DVR above the first extension is complete and weakly unramified over the lower coefficient DVR. The images of the remaining steps form a tower of the four types of length at most one less, by the base-change clause of the filtration lemma applied to the tower above the first step. Its residue field is finite over the original upper residue. The finite-extension perfect-core lemma says that its perfect core is algebraic over $k$; since $k$ is algebraically closed this core is $k$. Thus all hypotheses of the induction hold, including the perfect-core equality. Induction gives a finite solution $H_2/N_1$ for this chosen top branch.

source.place: Tag 09F8, induction paragraph; explicit verification of the omitted coefficient normal-closure and residue hypotheses.

proof.text: Enlarge $H_2$ to a finite normal $N_2/F$ separable over $H_2$ by coefficient-field arithmetic. On each branch already solved over $H_2$, the further extension $N_2/H_2$ is totally ramified and preserves index one by the totally ramified base-change lemma. Weak-solution descent assembles these two stages: at least one branch of the original top normalization over $N_2$ has index one over the lower coefficient DVR. Because $N_2/F$ is normal, branch conjugacy says every top branch has that same index. Hence $N_2/F$ solves the entire tower. This proves the induction and, by step 1, gives the required weak solution for $U\to W$. Normalization and descent also supply maximal contraction and the DVR conditions in the definition of weak solution.

source.place: Tag 09F8, induction paragraph and Tag 09EU; normalizing the final coefficient extension makes the conjugacy argument valid for every branch.

proof.text: Finally suppose $\operatorname{char}(F)=p$ and fix the specified uniformizer $t$ of $U$. Apply coefficient-field arithmetic to the finite extension $H/F$ just constructed: it writes this same field as $H=H_sF[t^{1/p^r}]$ with $H_s/F$ finite separable and $r\geq0$. The solution is unchanged, so its normalized branch conditions remain true. This proves the prescribed compositum clause without asserting that a weak solution survives arbitrary further extensions.

source.place: Tag 09F9, paragraph observing that every extension of k((t)) has the stated compositum form; Tag 09F8 final paragraph.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, proof; Tag 09F9, uniformizer-root compositum observation.
